We simplify the right-hand side:
\[
\frac{\cos 50^\circ}{1-\sin 50^\circ}
\]
Using the identity
\[
\frac{\cos \theta}{1-\sin \theta}=\frac{1+\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}=\tan\left(45^\circ+\frac{\theta}{2}\right),
\]
with \(\theta=50^\circ\), we get
\[
\frac{\cos 50^\circ}{1-\sin 50^\circ}
=\tan(45^\circ+25^\circ)
=\tan 70^\circ.
\]
So the equation becomes
\[
\tan(x-160^\circ)=\tan 70^\circ.
\]
Since tangent has period \(180^\circ\),
\[
x-160^\circ=70^\circ+180^\circ k
\]
for integer \(k\). Thus
\[
x=230^\circ+180^\circ k.
\]
For \(k=-1\), \(x=50^\circ\), which is positive. For \(k=0\), \(x=230^\circ\). Therefore, the smallest positive integer is \(50\).

The answer is 50.
